h1: Kenya business ETA from the UK
intro: Travelling to Kenya for meetings, a conference or a trade fair? This page explains the Kenya business ETA, who needs one and what to prepare. We check the rules for your passport and apply for you.
eligibility: You are travelling for meetings, conferences, trade fairs, negotiations or site visits
You won’t be paid by a company in Kenya
You have an invitation from the company or event you’re visiting

sections.heading: Do you need a Kenya business ETA?
sections.text: Kenya's Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) covers business visits as well as tourism. British passport holders apply online for an ETA before travelling.

sections.heading: What counts as a business visit?
sections.text:
Business visits usually include:
- Meetings with clients, suppliers or partners
- Conferences, exhibitions and trade fairs
- Negotiating or signing contracts
- Site visits and inspections

They don't include taking up paid work for a company in Kenya. That needs a work visa or permit.

sections.heading: Documents for a Kenya business ETA
sections.text: The key document is the invitation letter from the company you're visiting. It should include your name and passport number, the purpose and dates of your visit, the company's address and contact details, and who is paying for the trip. A letter from your UK employer confirming your role helps too.

sections.heading: Kenya business ETA help from Manchester
sections.text: We handle Kenya business ETA applications for individuals and companies across the UK, including urgent trips. See our [corporate visa services](/corporate-clients/) if your staff travel regularly. Before you travel, read the UK government's [foreign travel advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice) for Kenya.

faqs.q: Can I attend a conference on a Kenya business ETA?
faqs.a: Yes. Conferences, exhibitions and trade fairs are business visits.

faqs.q: Can I work in Kenya on a Kenya business ETA?
faqs.a: No. Being paid by a local company, or doing hands-on work, usually needs a work visa or permit.

faqs.q: What should the invitation letter include?
faqs.a: Your name and passport number, the purpose and dates of your visit, the company’s details, and who is paying for the trip.
